body:
**User impact:** #411 made merge mode fail closed when a wave PR's base isn't the bundle's resolved target base — the safe floor, and correct. But the guard that *prevents* wrong bases runs at publish time, so a PR created by an **earlier** run still carries the hazard. Switching an existing batch from stack mode to merge mode therefore turns every such PR into a manual stop: the operator is told what is wrong and left to fix each one by hand, even though the fix is mechanical.

### Proposal

When the merge-mode base check finds `baseRefName != resolved target base`:

1. attempt `gh pr edit <pr> --base <target-base>` and re-verify the base;
2. only if the retarget fails — no rights, branch gone, diff no longer applies — stop with the existing message naming both refs.

Retargeting at merge time heals PRs from earlier runs; pure refusal leaves them all as manual work. The refusal path stays exactly as #411 shipped it, as the fallback.

### Provenance

Recorded at pdca-pdca's sign-off of its issue_411 cycle (the fail-closed guard, PR #438) and kept until now only as a comment on the closed #411 (`https://github.com/eduralph/pdca-harness/issues/411#issuecomment-5198287452`). Re-filed as its own issue at the pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-08-10: a comment on a closed issue is not a tracked item, and this follow-up had been carried as "still open" across two reviews with nothing behind it.
